verdict.tagline: Survival crafting and monster collection marred by technical friction.
for_you_if: you want an expansive survival crafting sandbox
you enjoy automating resource gathering with monsters
not_for_you_if: you need polished performance and stable frame rates
you dislike heavy grind in late game regions

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players experience technical jank and frame drops while building bases and fighting tough bosses.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from technical jank, citing issues with movement, clunky controls, and buggy AI.

citations.review_text:
While the game mechanics feel pretty enjoyable, the game is just far too janky for my taste. There are some games that are made by a small studio and you can't tell, but in this game there are far too many telltale signs that tip off the player that this was a game made by a small studio. The movement is janky, there are countless quality of life mechanics that haven't been implemented, such as pinning recipes, and the story is obviously non-existed.

At it's core, I believe I would have liked this game but because of all of the annoyances in-between what this game could have been and the actual product, I can't recommend this game at all.

I really wanted to enjoy this, but it never clicked.

The biggest issue isn't the gameplay—it's the world itself. It feels lifeless. Outside of your base, there isn't much that makes the world feel like it's actually alive. NPCs are forgettable, the environment feels static, and the Pals quickly become little more than automated workers. Exploration was fun at first, but that sense of discovery faded much faster than I expected. It's just boring, and there is considerable jank in this game from the controls, buggy AI, general clunkiness of it all. 

The building and automation systems are decent, but they weren't enough to carry the experience for me because I never became invested in the world.

I also can't ignore the developer's track record. Craftopia showed a lot of promise but was largely left behind as attention shifted to Palworld. That makes it difficult for me to have confidence in the long-term support for this game.

It's clearly a game that many people enjoy, but if you're looking for a world that feels alive rather than just a sandbox full of mechanics, this may not click for you either.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game experiences performance issues and frame rate drops on specific hardware setups.

citations.review_text:
Game severely lacking optimization on AMD GPU's. It is a shame for such a good game, but I shouldn't get 45 FPS in fights with my 9070XT. It feels like playing a game on PS4 with 30FPS. Also UI is still too raw for a 1.0 release. The main issue is the lack of optimization for AMD hardware. I find it utterly disappointing and unbelievable in 2026. I can't recommend this game, unless they bring optimization for AMD GPU's. I will try to continue playing.

Edit: I am currently away from my PC, that's why I can't try any of these fixes. But I see all of your comments. Thank you for all the meaningful advices. I am also completely fine with trolling comments, but this review will surely help others, when they have similar issues such as myself. So please minimise the trolling.
this game is good but has cpu performance issues, with my i5 12400f at medium settings the fps drops bellow 30 fps in some areas. so if you have a very good cpu then you will be able to enjoy it

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the base building and automation system as a core feature where Pals can be assigned to tasks to help harvest, craft, and manage resources.

citations.review_text:
Palworld - 9/10, would exploit my Pals again
Went in expecting a Pokémon clone with guns, came out with a full-blown sweatshop simulator. 10/10 would enslave a Lamball again.
Grind is real but base building makes it worth it - slap down a base, put 15 Pals on manual labor, watch them mine/chop/cook while you go AFK. Capitalism simulator fr fr.
Combat actually slaps - guns + Pals + base building shouldn't work together but it does. Alpha bosses hit like a truck early game, ez clap once you're geared up.
Breeding is deep af for a "haha Pokémon but guns" meme game. Min-maxing Pal stats hits that same braindead-addictive itch as any good grindy sandbox.
Cons: performance can be sus depending on your rig, some jank, and the lawsuit jokes write themselves at this point ngl. Devs actually ship updates tho, rare W.
TL;DR: grind + base building + morally questionable labor practices involving cute creatures = peak. 9/10, Pal Union would like a word.

So, I purchased Palworld when it first came out. At the time, I didn't get it. I played for about an hour and decided to get a refund. I guess that's why they tell you you have to give games more time.  I saw that 1.0 was coming out and for some reason I started watching some videos. I gave the game another chance and I'm really glad I did. I won't talk about the graphics and that kind of stuff. You've seen that with your own eyes.  I will tell you that this game gets a huge thumbs up from me.

This has become one of those games for me where I just don't want to stop playing. There are so many things to do within the game. It's so much more than a simple building game. All the pals are different and the exploration is just a lot of fun. The base building is a lot of fun as well, as you try to figure out which pals do what and how that can help you throughout the game, not just in base building, but in fights, harvesting, collecting and other tasks.  I've never been much for Pokemon, but I can definitely see why Pocketpair won the legal battle because this game is so much more than Pokemon in my opinion.

It has a gamplay loop, but not one that becomes boring at all. There always seems to be a purpose for everything you do. The game has enough instruction and a guide where it's easy to pickup but challenging to master, at least for this older gamer.

If you're into survival, adventure and open world, this game does all these very well. I'm really glad I gave it another chance. If you've been on the fence, give this game some time. I think it will grow on you. I know it did me!

I went into Palworld not expecting much, but it ended up being one of those games that just hooks you for hours without you realizing it.

At the start, it feels like a pretty standard survival game: you’re gathering resources, crafting, and trying not to die. But once you get a bit further in, the whole system opens up. The base-building and automation is honestly where the game shines. Setting up your Pals to handle tasks for you makes progression feel really satisfying instead of just grindy.

The gameplay loop is simple but very addictive. You explore, catch Pals, expand your base, and keep upgrading everything. Then suddenly you look at the clock and it’s been 5 hours.

One thing I really like is how flexible the game is. You can tweak settings to make it more relaxed or more challenging, and it works both solo and with friends. It doesn’t force you into one playstyle.

Also, the world and creature designs are great. Everything looks light and fun on the surface, but there’s actually a decent amount of depth in how everything works together.

That said, it’s not perfect. The mid-game can slow down a bit, and some parts can feel repetitive after a while. But honestly, it never got to a point where I wanted to quit, especially since updates keep improving things.

Overall, it’s just a really solid and surprisingly deep game. If you’re into survival, base building, or creature collecting, it’s definitely worth trying. It’s one of those games that’s easy to pick up and hard to put down.

I only know Palworld from the 1.0 update and the changes that came with it, so I never played the game before the major improvements. However, based on the current version, Palworld is the BEST survival game I have played.

The biggest strength of Palworld is how well its different systems work together. The progression, resource management, base building, exploration, combat, and Pal mechanics are designed with a clear purpose and create a complete survival experience.

The automation system is one of the strongest parts of the game. Many survival games make automation unnecessarily complicated, but Palworld keeps the system simple and efficient. Assigning Pals to tasks, expanding production, and managing your base are straightforward while still allowing for advanced setups.

The progression system is also extremely well designed. The resources, technologies, and upgrades all contribute directly to improving your base, unlocking new possibilities, and advancing through the game. The grind is balanced because the effort directly results in meaningful upgrades.

Palworld combines survival, creature collection, automation, and open-world exploration in a way that avoids making any individual system overwhelming. Each mechanic supports the others and contributes to the overall experience.

I cannot comment on the state of the game before version 1.0, but the current version provides one of the most complete and well-executed survival experiences available.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that crafting and building recipes cannot be queued infinitely, requiring manual input for production tasks.

citations.review_text:
While the game mechanics feel pretty enjoyable, the game is just far too janky for my taste. There are some games that are made by a small studio and you can't tell, but in this game there are far too many telltale signs that tip off the player that this was a game made by a small studio. At it's core, I believe I would have liked this game but because of all of the annoyances in-between what this game could have been and the actual product, I can't recommend this game at all.

Baited in with "legally distinct pokemon with guns", dropped because of how grindy and micromanage-y it becomes already at around level 30-35 (took me about 14 hours to get there).

The game devolves from a fun exploration open world adventure game with neat base building mechanics by utilizing pals to having to micromanage multiple bases instead without providing you with the good enough logistics tools to properly establish or automate that.

My interpretation:
Need ore? Build another base.
Need coal? Build another base.
Need sulfur? Build another base.
Need breeding? Build another base.
Need food for all of those? Build farms and cookers in every base.
Need resources moved between them? Congratulations, you are the conveyor belt.
Need to start a new recipe (because you can't queue up recipes to be produced infinitely)? Nope - have to queue those up manually each time.

And yes, there are world settings that can be tweaked to make the game less grindy and more snappy but I expect a finished product out of the box that actually respects my time by providing curated content meant for the average Joe who doesn't want to micromanage 2-5 bases and stamp out hundreds if not thousands of the same material. Else why are there even presets to begin with?

Apart from the questionable design described above:
- The pal designs are very cool, especially when you find the bigger ones.
- The game runs well.
- The combat is basic but it works. Melee might need some tweaks to be more viable.
- The world feels lifeless for the most part but it's also passable.
- The UI is fine.
- Some people might find that the camera is too close to the character even at max FOV.

citations.review_text:
Alright, so I decided to try it out after everybody and their grandma praised it like crazy. The praise was definitely earned. It vaguely reminds me of Ark series married to Pokemon, but not like an arranged marriage full of indifference and monetary gain, but genuine love and respect. 

Ok, so gameplay.

 You're not blocked from exploring further than you want, though some npc's will warn you not to be a dumba** because 'there's really, REALLY high level pals over there I wouldn't recommend, friend' there is a stamina bar to watch for, but thankfully it doesn't make you have a full night sleep or chug potions to regain it. You have to watch for hunger, though it's fairly easy to manage. 

 Each pal has it's specialties, some are good mainly for combat and some are especially good for work at your base. You can be a cruel taskmaster or you can be a chill employer, it's your choice. Learn to dodge roll, it'll save your life, and don't risk anything for pals that are 3 levels above you, not unless you're reeeaaally prepared. Always have spheres at hand, there's always that one surprise pal you encounter and want. 

 Explore but remember to rank up your base too to unlock all the features.  

 All in all, good fun and time flies by very quick when you play Palworld

I'm not usually interested in survival games but having your pals help build, supply and run your base makes it feel much more alive than most survival games where you are doing everything alone and NPCs are usually just quest givers or shopkeepers and nothing else.
Actual combat is pretty simple, and I'd say primarily stat based.  If your numbers are big enough you can defeat most enemies with brute force and while it is possible to kill stronger enemies by dodging their attacks, against super strong enemies you'll do so little damage it will take ages and you can die to a single aoe attack.  That said, it's still pretty enjoyable and the massive number of passive and active skills you can give your pals can help keep combat from feeling too stale.
All in all, other games do individual aspects of this game better, but this game has so many combined things at least decently well that it's definitely a good deal if you enjoy the mixture of creature collecting, base building/management and upgrading/optimization of your pals.
I picked this up in early access on sale and since they did not increase the price at 1.0 launch there's no FOMO.  All in all it's a good bang for your buck game.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe experiencing crashes and technical instability, including Unreal crash reports with exception access violations when visiting certain areas or islands.

citations.review_text:
I have had more crashes in 1.0 15 hours than 50+ hours of early access... And glitches everywhere...
The game is less polished now then it was during early access...

I would love to play this game again, but after a certain point, I get consistent and unerring crashes from certain islands, with no clear indication other than EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION from the Unreal crash report. 

With the time I DID get to play with this game, it's an absolute blast, but ever since 1.0, I just can't play the game anymore without my game getting hardlocked to a certain point due to the consistent crashes that give no feedback as to the reason behind it, and once it happens while I'm within the island, I can't leave without crashing entirely, setting me back to square one of trying to leave, be it from Fast travelling, walking away, or emergency escape resets. 

I wanna love you Palworld, but you don't seem to wanna love me back.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that boss fights rely heavily on a strict time limit and DPS checks rather than complex environmental mechanics.

citations.review_text:
This game offers no challenge and is mostly a time sink. You cant get around battles by being clever, because every one of them is a stat check and bosses have a hard time limit that just kills you. You can tweak your chances with type advantage, but theres no clever strategy, you couldnt pull off a "beating pokemon emeral when every enemy is level 100" stuff. 

Base automation is alluring until you realize that theres a lot of repetitive tasks that you are stuck with always doing. Theres never a factorio style production chain that just spits out the finished product.

Also gameplay like, lets capture 64 identical pals to throw into the meatgrinder to make one pals stronger just isnt it. Thats boring grind. Another grind factor are those collectible statues, thats not exploration its just grazing on a too large map with too little going on.

So while the game is passable to spend some 20 hours with friends, it will never peak above a slow trickle of dopamin nor challenge you. Ultimately you will sit back at some point and realize the slowly creeping grind of the game has gotten too much to be enjoyable.

I'm mixed on this. Get this if you like exploring a world that's beautiful and just wandering around capturing a huge variety of pals. The crafting is interesting enough - though if you have zealous friends you get yanked up the tech tree and through content, which is something no game can really fix.
My biggest complaint is boss fights. They are supposed to be the pinnacle of any game and like most other games, this one just flops with them. While visually great - their mechanics are pure boring using the same sequences of moves making them predictable after the first cycle of what they can do. There's not a lot of environmental mechanics to deal with - mostly it's just a circular arena. Maybe you get pillars or rocks for cover.
The most soul sapping part is the timer - a 5 minute timer on boss fights means all your skill at dealing with mechanics, your clever use of environment and positioning to avoid damage, managing pals, all that means ultimately nothing to how much DPS you can throw downrange, making burst damage king.
May as well just set up a wooden dummy and measure my DPS for a minute, then give a pass/fail the boss fights suck the soul out of me in that manner. You either over level/over gear the fights or bring over leveled friends who just pound the boss into dirt with you, meaning what's the purpose of having a DPS check if you can just do that? I always view this as a lazy way to 'up difficulty' over interesting boss and environmental mechanics. The only strategy is if you take a pet with skills the boss is weak against. Of course this requires fore knowledge of what type the boss is to begin with taking that fun of going in blind out of the equation.

World and Crafting++ Great, even if the crafting is like any other survival game out there. Spend points on a tech tree - get the best gear - rinse and repeat. There are certain new toys you get that make it interesting to continually obtain materials and craft though. The variety of pals is prett…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that base automation requires constant manual supervision because crafting stations cannot queue recipes without ingredients present on the spot and lack the ability to set persistent minimum material stocks or prioritize specific work types for pals.

citations.review_text:
Overall its a really good game, I wish steam had a mixed review button here.

My biggest gripe with the game is the automation part.
Sure manually adding recipes and letting pals do the work seems to be fine, but I still wished I can put a minimum amount of wanted material on a crafting station so that its always topped up and so that pals would just yoink the required crafting mat out of the chests.

This game needs a serious overhaul. If I finish it anyway I'll update this review, but my frustrations with the game right now can be summed up pretty concisely: It tries to do so many things, that it doesn't do any individual thing well. 

My biggest issue with it is the base system, especially automation. I was going to use the word "encourages", but in fact the game forces you to use the automation system by imposing very high material requirements to make things, and long, long wait times to actually craft them. This alone shouldn't be a problem - I mean I play Satisfactory and Factorio, this should be my type of thing! But the automation is so poorly implemented that interfacing with it is just a chore. It requires endless micromanagement. You cannot queue recipes, meaning you need the ingredients to make something right there on the spot, and only then can you set the recipe and enable your pals to make the product. This means there is no full automation of any production chain. Every single step needs to be supervised. Secondly, it uses a Rimworld-style work type system for your pals, but does not let you prioritise work types at all. You can only tell them what they can and can't do, rather than what they should do first and last. 

This wouldn't be so bad if bases were bigger, you could have more of them, and more pals in them, but you can't. So you're stuck constantly changing out recipes and pals in the bases to keep inching through the progression. Every part of it feels like meaningless, arbitrary roadblocks thrown in front of you to drag the game out - and I'm not even at the end game yet which I'm painfully aware is just more of the same, yet even more sluggish. And yes I have been exploring in the meantime, and I have my issues with exploration too! As I said, it tries so many things that each one of them is lacking in thoughtful design. 

The only people I could possibly recommend the game to in this state, are people who enjoy the grind of Rust, Ar…

cohorts.summary: Long-term players note sparse late game zones, performance stuttering, and rigid keybindings.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the open world map features sparse, barren areas or empty feel in later regions compared to the starting zones.

citations.review_text:
Disappointing 1.0 Release

The devs took a very strange direction with the game. They decided to keep adding tons of content until it became extremely bloated instead of fixing core issues. 

- The open world still feels dead and empty.
- The base building is abysmal.
- The movement and animations are janky/unpolished.
- The combat mechanics lack any form of depth (the only interesting thing is certain Pals passive abilities)
- After 2 years the game is still horribly optimized. Loading screens take forever and graphics are decent at best.
- Most of the game is unnecessarily grindy and takes out any kind of "fun" there is.

This game had a lot of potential. It was pretty fun in early access, but 2 years later the game has not improved. 

4/10, there are many survival games on steam that are significantly higher quality.

If Palworld was still in early access, the current level of development would be justified. I'm sure it would be a game of all times if it spent a couple more years in the oven. Sadly, from what I've read, the developer doesn't plan on anything beyond fixing bugs and polishing the game, so I guess it's safe not to expect any massive reworks in the future.

My review is an honest compilation of my first impressions of the base game (no mods, Hard difficulty).

[h2]Content for the sake of content[/h2]
There is a difference between "an optional mechanic" and "unnecessary content bloat". I'd rather have a game with polished core gameplay than dilute it with every idea it can reach without much consideration about how well it synergizes with the rest of the gameplay. This results in the same eclectic feeling as seeing a screenshot of Skyrim with assault rifles, Ultrakill, and Terraria mods crammed into one frame, rather than a game built with a set goal in mind.

[h3]The map[/h3]
The starting area is the closest thing Palworld nails to perfection: it has both lvl 1 weaklings and lvl 34 behemoths, it's great to begin with and still has something to return for once the player leveled up. And then other areas drop the ball immediately.
The further you go into the game, the sparser the areas become. Islets are barren wastelands with 2-3 kinds of pals roaming around, copy-pasted enemy bases, and absolutely nothing else to do. Areas become increasingly strict about what lvl pals spawn there, which makes the open world less meaningful and only adds frustration to the exploration aspect. You find a new area, and your reaction is either "nothing useful for my lvl here" or "I'm too fresh to be here".
Level-gating areas this way only prohibits players from combat. Nothing prevented me from going into a lvl 65-70 skyland area when I was only 34, gathering the most powerful spheres from the ground, and catching pals who could one-shot me if I looked at them wrong.

claims.claim: Reviewers note issues with keybinding flexibility, specifically mentioning hardcoded keys or unchangeable default bindings such as the inventory key.

citations.review_text:
"The inventory can now be opened with the I key."

Reading through the 1.0 patch notes, I glanced at this but didn't think much of it.
After downloading the game again, I tweaked some world settings, made a character, and approached the first eagle statue to unlock fast travel-
And my character menu opened.

Checked settings. Scrolled through the options. Yeah, it's a shadow-bind, can't change it in settings.
Anytime you press I, the menu pops up.
Which wouldn't bother most players, pressing Tab also opens the menu. Redundant, sure, but who cares?

Well, me. I have left-handed keybinds. I don't use WASD. it's IJKL. So now, anytime I stop a forward movement, the menu opens.
I've enjoyed all the time I sunk into this game, and wanted to sink a hundred more hours.
It's the current year. There's no reason to have shadow binds that can't be swapped by the player.

Doesn't work on non en-US keyboards
Keys not bindable in the UI, most of them are hardcoded
Input.ini ignored by the game

The year is 2026 and somehow all these modern games (looking at you Grounded 1&2) have these issues that were already solved in the 90s by real PC devs

Edit: There is a mod to make this game playable for AZERTY and ESDF gamers on Nexusmods

Very fun game but the fact that the 1.0 release came out and I still cant change every keybind in the game is insanely frustrating. And on top of that now you can't even rebind the i key it seems like its always open inventory and I use that key for movement as a left handed player. I shouldn't rely on third party software to fix an issue that's been here since the very first release and now is ever worse in the 1.0 launch. I'll still play it's just very sad

The game isn't bad, there are plenty of options to spend your time on, from collecting all the Pals to base customisation, to fishing, to breeding the stats of a Pal to make it as best as possible. All are time intensive. The early game flashed by and then the mid to late to end game was an absolute crawl, if that. The OST is near non-existent unfortunately, the little that is there is okay. 

An interesting monster-collecting, base-building, open world experience. The combat is very simple, the type match-up chart is very basic, this is acceptable for the scope of the game as it currently stands. Pals can only have three moves at a time, however being able to swap out any they've learned on a whim is very welcome. Only having 5 slots in your proverbial party is a bit lacking for my tastes. I'd want a specific slot as a mount, for instance. Having to build a Pal purely as a mount takes one slot from you, or you just have a mount that isn't as fast as you'd like, but at least it can fight better. The performance on my machine never felt stable. On item pick up the game would always freeze frames no matter how much I lowered the settings. I'm assuming it's my machine, but it wasn't an enjoyable experience, it was always struggling, even if just flying around. There are some issues even in the v1.0 release, such as a collectable being lodged inside a rock, Pal habitat locations being incorrect in a few examples. I could never get foundations and structures in a base to actually work out. Pals would constantly get stuck even after their attempts at fixing things, even if I spaced the base out as much as possible and forewent building foundations and walls. The dev's workaround for this is just having Pals still work the stations but from elsewhere in the base because they couldn't make the model physically move up stairs or around objects.…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the end game requires significant grinding and specific loadouts to progress.

citations.review_text:
Big Congratz! to the PalWorld Team for bringing this early-access game to 1.0. Successes like PalWorld really shows that Indie Devs can acquire good funding from alternative sources and not sacrifice any good ideas just to turn a profit for shareholders. It is a beacon now for Indie Devs that want to break away from the console and mega-corp AAA market, and have limited funding options to break away, so thank you PalWorld!

As for the game, I was ~10 when the original Pokemon Red came out. From the day I got Red and got my first Charmander, I've wanted a game exactly like this. And putting it on top of an open-world survival-mechanic game that you can explore with your friends -- and one that deeply depends on utilizing all possible Pals in the game -- really shows how much consideration they put into the design of this game. Every single Pal is important and changes the direction of how you play -- Flying and mountable Pal types allow you to explore more, some focus on bonuses for Fishing, some provide specialty benefits to ranching, etc. There are definitely Pals that are requisite -- Anubis, Mau Cryst, etc. -- but you'll get those naturally while playing just from random eggs you find. However, exploring every single Pal's capabilities and strengths changes the entire way you play, and you'll find yourself doing that instead of hunting down that Rayquaza-like Worldboss. Powerful Pals might be great for fighting but terrible for any other thing in the game -- the Mau Cryst I mentioned above is necessary because it digs up money when working at your base so that you can buy horn and medical supplies in the early game and it is rather average at combat.   

They've really struck gold; the mechanics are good, easily modified to fit your playstyle through world configuration settings, provide extremely high levels of qualitative and quantitative re-play, you can do it all either online or offline, family-friendly... and now with the multi-pal global box there is a…

I got over 150 hours out of Palworld, so there's definitely a lot to enjoy. The world is fun to explore, there's plenty to do, and the progression is satisfying for a long time.

Unfortunately, the endgame is where the experience falls apart for me.

The biggest issue is base automation. The game encourages you to build multiple automated bases across the map, but in my experience the AI slows down or stops working properly when you're too far away. My ranches and production lines work great while I'm standing there, but as soon as I leave, production drops dramatically. That makes building multiple specialized bases feel largely pointless.

The Pal progression also becomes very grind-heavy. To get the best Pals you need to rank them up, breed or modify passives, and catch large numbers of duplicates. On top of that, high-level bosses often have low capture chances even with the best spheres, which can make progression feel more like repeating the same task until the RNG finally goes your way.

I had a lot of fun with the first 100+ hours, but the endgame systems stopped respecting my time. If the developers improve off-screen base simulation and reduce some of the reliance on RNG, I'd happily recommend it again.

Do you enjoy tedious grind like Mobile games? THIS is the game for you!
While initially fun at first, especially the pal catching mechanic (gotta catch em all!). Once you've caught most of them and when tech progression grinds to a halt and actively fights you every single upgrade, it's time to move onto a better game. You'll find yourself waiting for pals to craft resources, find you need other resources to craft resources to craft other higher resources which require more resources to build up to make the next resources. It's beyond ridiculous and just look at the amount of ingots in this game will tell you exactly how ridiculous they're willing to go.

Otherwise, pretty fun. Shame it was ruined by insane boredom you'll feel before you even reach the end.
There is a fun game here and if you enjoy tech tree grinding progression you'll find a good home here. I just wanted a fun open world pokemon-like catching game and I got what I wanted out of that. But the sour taste it's left in my mouth has left me not recommending this game. 
I want to finish the game, I don't want to fight it just to see the damn ending. I've seen the final battles and the required grinding to do it and it's NOT WORTH IT.

EDIT: I will add I am returning since buying it 2 years ago, I was disappointed to find not much had actually changed in regards to bugs/glitches/jank.

The first twenty or so hours of Palworld are genuinely great. Catching Pals, building your first base, watching your automation come together - it delivers on its premise and does so with real charm. The Pal mechanics are novel enough to carry you enthusiastically through the early game, and there is a satisfying loop in those opening hours that is hard to put down, especially with a group of friends to play with.

Then you hit level 30-40 and beyond, this is when the cracks appear.

The late game is, bluntly, busywork dressed as content. The automation systems that felt so rewarding to build gradually reveal themselves as insufficient for mid-late game crafting, which can often only be achieved through repetitive manual farming loops to get resources whose production cannot be automated. Version 1.0 made this worse rather than better, quietly inserting new intermediate materials into existing crafting chains, inflating recipes that were already expensive without adding anything meaningful to the experience. More grind to pad out gameplay, without any substantive/enjoyable new gameplay to offer.

Strip away the grind and the actual gameplay loop is surprisingly thin. Newer 1.0 zones bring new visuals but the same actions. New materials add steps to crafting chains without adding decisions worth making or gameplay that is at all distinct from what we already had. The World Tree is a new area in the way a longer queue is a new experience compared to a shorter queue.

If you go in expecting a deep late game, you will be disappointed. If you go in expecting twenty to thirty hours of genuinely fun survival crafting with a fresh twist, Palworld delivers that honestly. With a little luck, the devs will improve the issues I mentioned here. I can still recommend as pricing is reasonable, and there's fun to be had earlier on before too many manual farming loops are constantly necessitated to ungate progress, especially in coop :)
